question: How do state-of-the-art computer-use (GUI) agents achieve accurate and fast desktop control, and which techniques could improve a macOS MCP server combining accessibility tree, OCR and screenshots?

include: agents that operate graphical user interfaces (desktop, web or mobile) from screenshots, accessibility trees or both
GUI grounding / screen parsing models and methods (mapping instructions to screen elements or coordinates)
benchmarks and empirical evaluations of computer-use agents (success rates, failure analysis, efficiency)
techniques that reduce model calls or latency for GUI agents (multi-action, API calls, caching, memory, replay)
security of GUI/computer-use agents (prompt injection, pop-ups, unsafe actions)
exclude: agents without a graphical interface (pure text/tool APIs, code agents)
UI design generation or UI code generation
position papers without method or evaluation

subquestions.text: Perception and grounding: how do agents find the right element (screenshots, accessibility tree, hybrids, set-of-marks, grounding models, zooming)?
Speed and efficiency: what reduces the number of model calls and latency (multi-action execution, API-first actions, workflow memory, trajectory replay)?
Reliability: how are computer-use agents evaluated (OSWorld, macOS, Windows benchmarks), where do they fail, and which methods (reflection, planning) improve success?
Safety: what attacks and risks affect computer-use agents (prompt injection, pop-ups) and which defenses exist?
